grammar.title: 有／沒(有)辦法 + 動詞 (to have / not have a way to do something)
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 有／沒(有)辦法 + 動詞 + (賓語)
grammar.explanation: 辦法 means "a way / a method". Put 有 or 沒(有) in front of it to say whether you are able to do something because of the situation (time, money, weather, ability of the moment). 想辦法 means "to think of a way". Note that 辦法 always needs a verb like 有／沒有／想 in front of it.
grammar.contrast: 沒辦法 vs 不會／不能: 不會 means you lack the skill (我不會游泳), 不能 means you are not permitted, and 沒辦法 means the circumstances leave you no way out (今天太忙，我沒辦法去). If the blocker is the situation, use 沒辦法.
grammar.common_error: Learners drop the verb in front of 辦法 and say 我辦法解決 or 我不辦法去. You must say 我沒辦法解決 / 我沒辦法去, or 我想辦法解決.

examples.hanzi: 我今天有事，沒辦法跟你去看電影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu shì, méi bànfǎ gēn nǐ qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.gloss: I'm busy today, so I can't go see a movie with you.

examples.hanzi: 這個問題太難了，我沒辦法解決。

passage.title: 悠遊卡不見了
passage.hanzi: 上個星期，我的悠遊卡不見了。我很擔心，因為卡裡還有一些錢。我先問車站的人，他說我可以到捷運站的服務台辦。這件事看起來很難，其實很快就解決了。現在我出門都會注意，不再讓它不見。
passage.gloss: Last week my EasyCard went missing. I was worried, because there was still some money on the card. First I asked someone at the station, and he said I could take care of it at the service counter in the MRT station. The whole thing looked hard, but actually it was solved very quickly. Now I pay attention whenever I go out, so I won't lose it again.

grammar.title: 被字句：說「誰被怎麼樣了」
grammar.pattern: 受事 + 被 (+ 做事的人) + 動詞 + 了／結果
grammar.explanation: 用「被」的時候，句子前面的人或東西是「事情發生在它身上」的那一個。做事的人可以說出來，也可以不說。動詞後面常常要加「了」或一個結果（走、完、到），不能只有一個光光的動詞。這個說法多半用在不好的、讓人擔心的事。
grammar.contrast: 最容易跟「使」弄錯。「被」：主語是受害的一方（我的腳踏車被人騎走了）。「使」：主語是原因，後面接一個人和他的感覺或改變（這件事使我很擔心）。問自己：前面那個是「被動了手腳的東西」還是「造成影響的原因」。
grammar.common_error: Learners leave the verb bare — saying 我的手機被拿 instead of 我的手機被帶走了. In Chinese a 被 sentence almost always needs 了 or a result ending on the verb. Learners also overuse 被 for neutral or happy events (我被老師教中文); for those, just use a normal active sentence.

examples.hanzi: 我的腳踏車被人騎走了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiǎotàchē bèi rén qí zǒu le.

passage.title: 夜市裡的小事
passage.hanzi: 上個週末，我和朋友去台北的夜市逛。走到一半，我發現錢包不見了。朋友問我，是不是被人帶走了？我很擔心，因為裡面有悠遊卡和一千多塊錢。後來，那家店的老闆出現了，手上就是我的錢包。這件事使我很感動，也影響了我對台灣人的看法。
passage.gloss: Last weekend I went with a friend to walk around a night market in Taipei. Halfway through, I discovered my wallet was gone. My friend asked me whether someone had taken it. I was really worried, because inside were my EasyCard and over a thousand dollars. Later, the owner of that shop appeared, and in his hand was my wallet. This really moved me, and it also changed the way I see Taiwanese people.

grammar.title: 把-sentences: saying what you did to a thing
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 把 + (特定的)東西 + 動詞 + 在/給/走/好/了
grammar.explanation: Use 把 when you move or change a specific, already-known thing. The thing goes right after 把, and the verb must be followed by a result: a place (放在桌上), a receiver (給我), or a resultative word like 走、好、了. 把 is very common with 放、拿、接、用 because these verbs naturally end in a result or a location.
grammar.contrast: 把 vs 被: both put the object before the verb, but 把 keeps the doer as the subject (我把傘拿走了 = I took it), while 被 makes the thing the subject (傘被他拿走了 = it was taken by him). Ask yourself who is doing the action — that decides which one you need.
grammar.common_error: Learners stop the sentence too early, saying 我把書放 or 我把手機拿. A 把 sentence always needs something after the verb (在桌上, 給我, 走, 好, 了). Also, 把 cannot be used with verbs that don't change anything, so 我把這本書看 / 我把他喜歡 are wrong.

examples.hanzi: 我已經把書放在桌上了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ shū fàng zài zhuō shàng le.
examples.gloss: I've already put the book on the table.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shǒujī gěi wǒ yíxià.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ wǒ de sǎn ná zǒu le.

grammar.title: 用 + tool + verb: doing something with something
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 用 + 工具 + 動詞 + 賓語
grammar.explanation: 用 introduces the tool or means before the main verb: 我用悠遊卡搭捷運, 她用手機打電話. The 用-phrase always comes before the verb it helps, never after.
grammar.contrast: 用 vs 把: 用 marks the tool you use, 把 marks the thing you move or change. 我用手機接電話 (tool = phone) vs 我把手機放在桌上 (the phone is what gets moved).
grammar.common_error: Learners put 用 after the verb, like 我搭捷運用悠遊卡. In Chinese the tool phrase must come first: 我用悠遊卡搭捷運。

passage.title: 週末接朋友
passage.hanzi: 週末早上，我把家裡的東西都放好，就出門了。我用悠遊卡搭捷運，到台北車站接我的朋友。她帶了一個很大的袋子，很重，我幫她拿。我們把袋子放在椅子旁邊，坐下來喝茶。後來我們走路去附近的書店，她買了一本書，說要送給我。
passage.gloss: Weekend: Picking Up a Friend — On Saturday morning I put everything at home away and headed out. I used my EasyCard to take the MRT to Taipei Main Station to pick up my friend. She had brought a very big bag, and it was heavy, so I carried it for her. We set the bag down beside a chair and sat down for some tea. Later we walked to a nearby bookstore, where she bought a book and said she wanted to give it to me.
